page: Microsoft Azure D128lds_v7 is a compute-optimized server instance from the Dldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 128 virtual CPUs across 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 7559 GB disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the D128lds_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance in multi-core processing and memory bandwidth. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test, PassMark CPU score, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all rank in the top 10% of tested instances. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks (10709.34 GB/sec) and large uncached blocks (657.87 GB/sec read, 254.77 GB/sec write) also place in the top 10%. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test and PassMark memory score landing in the middle 50%. The processor's advanced instruction support, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), contributes to top-tier results in ray tracing, text processing, and software compilation.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the D128lds_v7 is its low memory density relative to its massive compute capacity. While the 128 vCPUs provide substantial parallel processing power, the 256.0 GB of RAM may limit memory-intensive applications. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this resource distribution makes the instance highly efficient for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints, avoiding the premium associated with high-RAM configurations. The inclusion of 7559 GB of local storage, combined with top-tier performance in database operations (34662.86 operations in PassMark) and Redis SET operations (196.23 million operations/sec), makes this server suitable for high-throughput database hosting, static web serving, software compilation, and CPU-based LLM prompt processing.
